description: Business requirements for VRF architecture extension. No RT/RD values are provided — you must design an assignment scheme that satisfies all constraints using the existing RT/RD mappings in topology.json as context.

R1:QUARANTINE.purpose: Security quarantine zone for compromised hosts requiring remediation access through the management plane
constraints: Must receive management infrastructure routes leaked from the MGMT VRF on R1 so quarantined hosts can be remotely remediated
Must be completely invisible to the customer-facing CUST VRF on R1 — no QUARANTINE routes may appear in CUST's routing table under any circumstances
Must not inject any routes back into the MGMT VRF to prevent quarantined hosts from advertising rogue routes to management infrastructure
Must use explicit VPN route-leak semantics (rd vpn export, rt vpn export, rt vpn import, export vpn, import vpn) — do not use the import vrf shortcut

R2:MONITOR.purpose: Centralized network monitoring VRF aggregating routes for traffic analysis and observability tooling
constraints: Must aggregate routes from both the CUST VRF and the INTERNAL VRF on R2 for comprehensive network visibility
Must not inject any monitoring infrastructure routes back into the CUST VRF
Must not inject any monitoring infrastructure routes back into the INTERNAL VRF
Must use explicit VPN route-leak semantics (rd vpn export, rt vpn export, rt vpn import, export vpn, import vpn) — do not use the import vrf shortcut

design_evaluation_requirements.description: Produce a security assessment of the complete VRF route-leak architecture including all original VRFs (after bug fixes) and newly designed VRFs
deliverables: Identify any VRF that has route exposure beyond its minimum operational need
Identify any VRF pairs where bidirectional route leaking could create a lateral movement risk
Assess whether the RT assignment scheme follows minimum-privilege principles
Provide at least two concrete recommendations for improving the architecture's security posture
